title: Renewal & Expansion check-in - Stellar Med

Ravi to share recent dedicated vs hosted latency/cost benchmark spreadsheet and notes by 2026-09-16
Sana to schedule pilot test window (2 weeks) starting 2026-09-28
Tom to confirm internal procurement timeline and PO requirement by 2026-09-20
action_items: Maxine: prepare committed capacity pricing + add-on for burst/backstop, due 2026-09-17
Ravi: export dedicated vs hosted perf spreadsheet + KV cache notes, due 2026-09-16

summary: Renewal check-in with Stellar Med discussing renewal, committed capacity upgrade to 3 regions, pilot for dedicated nodes, and contract extension options. Actions: pricing, benchmarks, pilot schedule, procurement next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Maxine Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today. Quick check-in — renewing contract in Q4, and then scope for expansion across regions and capacity.
[00:12] Elena Garcia: Yes hi, thanks. We wanted to talk through two things: 1) committed capacity upgrade — we are seeing higher traffic for the notes summarization and clinical QA, and 2) adding EU region for data residency.
[00:25] Ravi Patel: Got it. Can you remind me current setup? Hosted or dedicated?
[00:29] Mark Liu: We're on hosted right now, small committed bundle, mostly us-east. Latency's okay for web but our batch jobs are hitting limits during morning syncs.
[00:38] Sana Ahmed: We also saw a couple of spikes where KV cache miss rate increased; want to understand autoscale + dedicated pools.
[00:46] Maxine Carter: Makes sense. Our recommended path is a move to Dedicated for predictable throughput — can pin capacity, set autoscale policy, and isolate data. But we also have a hybrid where critical routes hit Dedicated and others remain Hosted.
[00:58] Elena Garcia: What's the rough delta on cost? We need to justify to finance — cost per token vs current hosted.
[01:05] Ravi Patel: Rough back-of-envelope: Dedicated lowers per-token unit cost at higher throughput but has monthly reserved commit. There is a trade-off — we can model TCO with your traffic shape. I can send a spreadsheet.
[01:16] Mark Liu: Can you also include quantization impact? We used a 4-bit quantized variant in dev and saw small quality changes.
[01:22] Ravi Patel: Yup — the Optimize team has quant profiles. I'll include recommended profiles by workload (summarization vs classification).
[01:28] Sana Ahmed: Also need to check SSO/SCIM + audit logs for compliance. We're SOC 2 in flight and ISO is a possible ask.
[01:35] Maxine Carter: Totally — we have SOC 2 Type II and SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, audit logs, and KMS integrations. I'll attach the security pack — but if you want a deeper compliance review we can set up JG from our security team.
[01:47] Tom Reyes: From procurement, timeline — we need options for a 12-month extension or multi-year with discount tiers. Also need PO template and any required SLAs.
[01:55] Maxine Carter: For sure. We offer committed capacity contracts (monthly/annual), and multi-year discounts. I'll include the legal/Pricing options.
[02:03] Elena Garcia: For regions, we need EU and APAC. Do you have capacity in eu-west-1 and ap-south-1?
[02:09] Ravi Patel: We can provision in eu-west-1 and ap-south-1 but capacity lead times vary — depending on GPU pools. For Dedicated you can reserve across regions. We can also do cross-region fallback routing.
[02:20] Mark Liu: One concern — if we go Dedicated in EU, we need to know key management options (bring-your-own-key).
[02:26] Maxine Carter: BYOK via customer KMS/HSM is available in Private and Dedicated; Hosted also supports KMS but not customer HSM in some regions — I'll call that out in the doc.
[02:36] Sana Ahmed: For the pilot we want to run latency and cost benchmarks against our real traffic: p95 target under 450ms for short prompts and sustained throughput at 120 req/s for batch scoring.
[02:45] Ravi Patel: Good, we can set a 2-week pilot on Dedicated nodes with your traffic replayed. We'll capture token costs, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and model output diffs.
[02:54] Mark Liu: Any change in model variants or fallback behavior when capacity is constrained? We want graceful degradation.
[03:00] Ravi Patel: Redwood has routing policies — you can route by latency or cost; fallback to cheaper/quantized variant automatically. We'll show default policies and you can customize.
[03:09] Elena Garcia: Are there any customers doing similar multi-region Dedicated rollouts?
[03:13] Maxine Carter: Yes — a couple of healthcare customers have done EU + US Dedicated with BYOK and audit log retention — we can anonymize and share patterns.
[03:21] Tom Reyes: Legal — any data processing agreement or standard data residency language?
[03:25] Maxine Carter: We'll include DPA templates and standard data residency terms. For custom residency we can go to Private.
[03:32] Mark Liu: Benchmark specifics — will Ravi be able to share the exact test harness? 
[03:36] Ravi Patel: I'll share the benchmark harness and the spreadsheet with cost-model columns (token count, seq len distribution, batch sizing, KV cache hit assumptions).
[03:44] Elena Garcia: On the price side — how do burst/overage work if committed capacity is exhausted? We need backstop so our service doesn't degrade.
[03:52] Maxine Carter: There's burst credit and on-demand fallback; you can also set hard caps. We'll include burst pricing in the options.
[03:58] Sana Ahmed: Could you include the console screenshots for route-level cost breakdowns? Our ops team wants visibility.
[04:04] Maxine Carter: Yep, will send console screenshots and the per-route analytics export.
[04:09] Mark Liu: Any latency differences by quantization? For summarization quality is sensitive.
[04:14] Ravi Patel: For summarization we usually recommend FP16 or 8-bit quant for minimal quality loss. 4-bit can be okay for classification, but we'll include eval delta numbers.
[04:24] Elena Garcia: We also had internal question about model version pinning during rollout — can we pin to a model and perform canary rolls?
[04:29] Maxine Carter: Yes, rollouts support canary and A/B, automatic fallback policies, and version pinning.
[04:35] Tom Reyes: Procurement again — any standard SLA for latency?
[04:39] Maxine Carter: SLA is uptime-focused, but we can discuss latency SLOs in the dedicated contract. We'll map p95 targets to an SLO.
[04:47] Sana Ahmed: For the pilot success criteria, we'll define a cost per 1M tokens threshold and p95 latency. Also need regression checks on generation quality.
[04:56] Ravi Patel: We'll include eval harness to run quality regression and tie alerts to prompt sets.
[05:02] Elena Garcia: Great. Let's talk timing: renewal date is 2026-10-15 — we need to finalize terms 30 days before so finance can approve.
[05:11] Maxine Carter: Ok — timeline noted. We'll aim to get pricing and benchmark docs to you by 9/17 so you can review and schedule the pilot to start the week of 9/28.
[05:20] Mark Liu: For the multi-region capacity, what's the lead time to provision Dedicated GPUs?
[05:24] Ravi Patel: Typically 2-3 weeks depending on region and SKU; if you commit we can prioritize provisioning.
[05:30] Tom Reyes: Are there options to add capacity mid-term if we exceed commit?
[05:34] Maxine Carter: Yes — you can add burst capacity, or top-up committed nodes; pricing pro-rated.
[05:39] Elena Garcia: Competitor check — how do you compare to Anthropic and OpenAI on private deployment options?
[05:44] Maxine Carter: We focus on unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private with first-class observability and routing controls. We'll share a short comparison doc.
[05:52] Sana Ahmed: One last technical: KV cache persists between requests in Dedicated? We need to understand memory/caching for long-running sessions.
[05:58] Ravi Patel: KV cache persists per-session within the serving runtime; Dedicated gives more predictable cache sizing. We'll include memory sizing guidance.
[06:07] Elena Garcia: Ok good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:10] Maxine Carter: None. We'll gather docs and pricing.
[06:13] Tom Reyes: We'll follow-up with procurement timeline; I might need a vendor questionnaire answered.
[06:17] Maxine Carter: Send it over, we'll loop legal.
[06:20] Jess Nguyen: Quick recap of actions — Maxine pricing, Ravi benchmarks and harness, Sana pilot criteria, Tom procurement checklist.
[06:28] Elena Garcia: Yep that's it. Thanks everyone.
[06:31] Maxine Carter: Thanks — I'll follow up with an email and the attachments.
[06:34] Mark Liu: Bye.
[06:35] [call ends]
